title: Range queries: prefix, sparse table, Fenwick/BIT, segment tree (lazy stretch)
relevance: High — static range aggregates, point-update range queries, and inversion / order-statistic counting are staples of OAs and Div2 C–D; Fenwick + basic segtree are the interview DS upgrade past plain prefix sums.
company_notes: Design NumArray with point update and range sum → LC 307 / CSES Dynamic Range Sum (Amazon/Meta-style API). Count inversions / smaller to the right → LC 315 / Fenwick or merge sort (classic hard OA). Many static range min/max or XOR queries → sparse table or prefix XOR (CSES Static RMQ / Range Xor). First seat/hotel/server that can take load x then decrease capacity → Hotel Queries / walk-on-segtree.

phases.goal: Map the prompt to prefix, sparse table, Fenwick/BIT, segment tree, or lazy from static vs updates and the aggregate type.

must_hit.point: Static sum/XOR → prefix; static min/max/GCD → sparse table; once updates appear → Fenwick or segment tree.
must_hit.evidence_hint: States that three-way split from the checklist: prefix for static sum/XOR, sparse for static idempotent, tree when updates exist.

must_hit.point: Signal words: many queries on [l,r], update index then re-query, k-th element in a multiset, count inversions / nested segments, assign to first hotel with enough rooms.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Lists those signal phrases and ties them to range-query DS rather than naive scans.

must_hit.point: “Design NumArray: update index, query range sum” or “count inversions / how many smaller to the right” are core OA shapes for Fenwick/segtree (LC 307 / LC 315).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Names NumArray-with-updates or count-smaller-after-self and reaches for Fenwick or segtree.

must_hit.point: Range updates with range queries → lazy propagation (stretch); arbitrary associative merges or “walk to first index with …” → segment tree.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Separates lazy RURQ stretch from basic PURS and names walk-on-segtree for first-feasible index.

probes: Static range sum vs static range min vs point-update range sum—what structure do you pick for each?
What wording pushes you from prefix/sparse table into Fenwick, segtree, or lazy?

hints.1: Ask whether the array changes and whether the op is sum/XOR or min/max/GCD.
hints.2: Static sum/XOR → prefix; static idempotent → sparse; updates → Fenwick/segtree; walk-first / custom merge → segtree; RURQ → lazy stretch.
hints.3: Say: static sum/XOR → prefix; static min/max/GCD → sparse table; updates → Fenwick or segtree; NumArray/inversions → Fenwick/segtree; first hotel ≥ x → walk segtree; range update+query → lazy.

phases.goal: State the right structure and query/update plan before coding templates.

must_hit.point: Static + idempotent (min/max/GCD) → sparse table: O(1) query after O(n log n) preprocess, using two overlapping blocks of length 2^{floor(log(r−l+1))}.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Names sparse table for idempotent aggregates and the two-block O(1) query idea.

must_hit.point: Point updates + range sum → Fenwick (BIT) or segment tree; Fenwick range is sum(r) − sum(l−1).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Chooses BIT/segtree for PURS and writes the two-prefix difference for range sum.

must_hit.point: Arbitrary associative merges or walk-to-first-index → segment tree with associative merge (sum, min, XOR, or a struct).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Says segtree when merge is custom or you descend for first index with a property.

must_hit.point: Fenwick as frequency / order statistic: compress values, add(pos, ±1), find k-th by binary lifting on prefix sums (List Removals / Multiset).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Describes compress + ±1 freq BIT and k-th via prefix binary lifting.

probes: When is sparse table enough, and when must you switch to Fenwick or a segment tree?
How do you use a Fenwick as an order-statistic structure for k-th / inversions?

hints.1: Separate static idempotent from point-update sum and from walk/custom merge.
hints.2: Sparse for static min/max/GCD; BIT/segtree for PURS; freq BIT for k-th/inversions; segtree for walk/custom merge.
hints.3: Say: sparse O(1) after O(n log n) with two overlapping 2^{floor(log(r−l+1))} blocks; PURS via BIT/segtree with sum(r)−sum(l−1); compress+±1 BIT for k-th; segtree merge/walk for first ≥ x.

phases.goal: Confirm Fenwick bit tricks, sparse-table recurrence, segtree template, walk descent, and lazy tags.

must_hit.point: Fenwick is 1-indexed: add(i,δ) via i += i & −i; sum(i) via i −= i & −i; always long long on CF.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Recites the i & −i loops for add/sum and mentions 1-indexing plus long long.

must_hit.point: Sparse table build: st[k][i] = op(st[k−1][i], st[k−1][i+2^{k−1}]); query with two overlapping power-of-two blocks.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Writes that recurrence and the two-block idempotent query.

must_hit.point: Segment tree template: build / point-update / range-query with associative merge; iterative or recursive both fine.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Sketches build, point update, range query sharing one merge function.

must_hit.point: Walk/descent: first index with tree[node] ≥ x (Hotel Queries / CF EDU “first at least X”).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Describes descending the max (or similar) tree to the leftmost feasible leaf.

must_hit.point: Lazy (stretch): store pending add/assign tags; push before recursing; compose tags correctly (assign kills prior adds).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Mentions push-before-recurse and that assign overrides earlier add tags.

probes: Write the Fenwick add and prefix-sum loops using i & −i.
How do you build a sparse table, and how does Hotel Queries walk the segment tree?

hints.1: Start from 1-index Fenwick loops, then sparse recurrence, then segtree merge/walk.
hints.2: i += i&−i / i −= i&−i; st[k][i] from two half-length blocks; merge on segtree; descend for first ≥ x; lazy push + assign kills adds.
hints.3: Spell: 1-indexed BIT add/sum with i&−i and long long; st[k][i]=op(st[k−1][i], st[k−1][i+2^{k−1}]); segtree build/point-update/range-query; walk first tree[node]≥x; lazy tags with push and assign killing prior adds.

phases.goal: Anchor sparse-table and updateable-tree costs to the bounds stated in the topic.

must_hit.point: Sparse table answers idempotent range queries in O(1) after O(n log n) preprocess.
must_hit.evidence_hint: States O(n log n) build and O(1) query for static min/max/GCD.

must_hit.point: With n ≤ 2·10^5, Fenwick/segtree solutions must stay O((n+q) log n); naive per-query scans are too slow.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Cites the n ≤ 2·10^5 constraint and the O((n+q) log n) target for updateable structures.

probes: What are sparse-table preprocess and query costs for static RMQ?
Under n ≤ 2·10^5 with updates, what total complexity do you need from Fenwick or a segment tree?

hints.1: Contrast static sparse-table costs with online updateable trees under large n.
hints.2: Sparse: O(n log n) then O(1); with updates and n ≤ 2·10^5 stay O((n+q) log n).
hints.3: Say: sparse table O(n log n) preprocess, O(1) idempotent query; Fenwick/segtree under n ≤ 2·10^5 in O((n+q) log n) only.

phases.goal: Catch indexing, overflow, missing compression, wrong structure choice, and lazy tag composition bugs.

must_hit.point: Off-by-one on inclusive [l,r] and 0- vs 1-indexing; Fenwick must stay 1-indexed.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Calls out inclusive bounds and BIT 1-indexing explicitly.

must_hit.point: Overflow on CF: always use long long for Fenwick/prefix-style sums under contest constraints.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Insists on long long for BIT/range sums on Codeforces.

must_hit.point: Values up to 10^9 need coordinate compression before BIT/segtree (Salary Queries, inversions).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Compresses to ranks before building a frequency BIT when values are huge.

must_hit.point: Lazy tag mistakes: forgetting push before recursing, or composing add/assign wrong—assign must kill prior adds.
must_hit.evidence_hint: States push-before-child and assign overriding earlier adds.

probes: What indexing and overflow bugs show up first when coding a Fenwick?
When must you compress, and what goes wrong with lazy add vs assign composition?

hints.1: Check inclusive bounds, BIT base index, 64-bit sums, compression, and lazy push/compose.
hints.2: [l,r] inclusive; Fenwick 1-indexed; long long on CF; compress 10^9 values; push before recurse; assign kills adds.
hints.3: Say: inclusive [l,r] and 1-indexed BIT; always long long on CF; compress values up to 10^9; lazy push before recursing and let assign kill prior adds.

tradeoffs.topic: Prefix sums vs sparse table vs Fenwick/segment tree
tradeoffs.strong_answer: Static sum/XOR → prefix; static min/max/GCD → sparse table O(1) after O(n log n); once point updates appear → Fenwick or segment tree.
Point updates + range sum (or XOR-as-sum) → either Fenwick or segtree; arbitrary associative merges, custom node structs, or walk-to-first-index (≥ x) → segment tree.

tradeoffs.topic: Plain PURS tree vs lazy propagation
tradeoffs.strong_answer: Point update / range query stays with basic Fenwick or segtree; range updates with range queries need lazy tags (stretch)—push before recursing and compose so assign kills prior adds.

tradeoffs.topic: Sparse table vs segment tree for static RMQ
tradeoffs.strong_answer: If the array never changes and the op is idempotent (min/max/GCD), sparse table is the O(1)-query choice; if updates or non-idempotent/custom merges appear, use a segment tree instead.

gotchas.trap: Scanning each [l,r] query when many queries ask for an associative aggregate.
gotchas.correction: Precompute or maintain a structure: prefix, sparse table, Fenwick, or segment tree depending on static vs updates.

gotchas.trap: Using a sparse table when the array must support updates.
gotchas.correction: Sparse table is for static idempotent queries; switch to Fenwick or segment tree once updates appear.

gotchas.trap: 0-indexing a Fenwick or mixing inclusive [l,r] bounds.
gotchas.correction: Keep Fenwick 1-indexed; add via i += i & −i, sum via i −= i & −i; range = sum(r) − sum(l−1).

gotchas.trap: Building a BIT/segtree on raw values up to 10^9 for frequency / order-statistic queries.
gotchas.correction: Coordinate-compress first (Salary Queries, inversions), then add(pos, ±1) and query ranks.

gotchas.trap: Overflow on Codeforces with Fenwick or long prefix sums.
gotchas.correction: Always use long long for these structures under CF constraints.

gotchas.trap: Lazy add/assign composed incorrectly or push skipped.
gotchas.correction: Push pending tags before recursing; assign kills prior adds when composing tags.
